about: What changed, in words for friends, newest first. Add a line to the top entry as things merge; start a new entry (the next id) after a release. Each release's notes start with the entries it adds, and the app shows people the ones they haven't seen.

items: Going back to a room shows it at once, right where you were reading.
Point at someone's name for a moment to see who they are and message them. Ctrl+K can now do things too, like inviting people or joining the fire.
Messages show up the moment you send them, faded until they're delivered, with Try again if one doesn't go through.
When two friends sit down at a fire, the rest of the hearth gets a note with a Join button. Set a hearth to only @mentions to turn it off.
Right-click a hearth to mark it as read, or press Shift+Esc. Alt+Shift+↓ now jumps to the next unread room in any hearth.
Deleting your own message no longer asks first. You get a few seconds to undo it instead.
If you lose your connection for more than a few seconds, a bar at the top says so, with a button to try again. Messages waiting to send show greyed out in the chat.
Messages has a proper empty screen until you start a conversation, and a new hearth has an Invite friends button.
In the desktop app, the update button lists what the new version brings, and "What's new" waits until you've updated.
New hearths start with a Campfire. If the voice server can't be reached, joining a fire says so, with Try again.
Peiskos tells you when you're removed from a hearth or it's deleted, and when the room you're typing in goes away (your unsent message can be copied).
_Underscores_ make italics too, and editing a long message gives you a box big enough to see it.

Emoji look the same for everyone now, on every device: Peiskos draws them with Google's Noto emoji instead of your device's own. Flags show on Windows too. While you type, the message box still uses your device's emoji.

Pop out the game you're playing into its own window, from the button next to Back to the fire: the casino, Fireside Angler, Stockpile or Melon Bomber (between rounds). In the desktop app the pin keeps it on top.
Confirmations and errors are Peiskos's own now, instead of your browser's pop-ups. Deleting a hearth asks you to type its name.
A hearth's settings, Your account and Server admin are one page each, with sections down the side. On phones, a hearth's settings start as a list.
New friends get a short welcome: a picture and name, alerts, and a mic check. Every step can be skipped.
Rooms show placeholders while they load, and messages show just the time under the date line.
Light, dark or match your device is in Your account › Settings.
